headline: The same density behind Ward 43's historic buildings also explains its parking shortage.
summary:
Ward 43 holds 1,531 buildings logged in Chicago's historic resources survey, more than any other ward in the city, and City Council added three more protections this spring when it landmarked artist Roger Brown's former home and two DePaul University buildings in Lincoln Park. That same tightly built, historic footprint also puts Ward 43 first among the 48 wards measured for licensed music and dance venues per resident, a concentration dense enough that a single electronic music festival in June turned into a fight over a possible ward-wide noise ban. Density like that has a cost. Ward 43 ranks 48th of 50 for how many residential blocks are crowded enough to need permit parking, a direct read on how hard curb space is to find, and residents got a preview of that scarcity in July, when a Pride Parade towing sweep caught drivers who said the no-parking signs went up without enough warning.

Three of Ward 43's other top scores are not counted from anything happening in the ward itself. Childhood lead levels, social cohesion, and social support are all allocated from census tract data, assigned by geography rather than measured door to door, and the source attaches a confidence grade to all three, low on one and medium on the other two. The same kind of number sits near the bottom of the list. A modeled estimate of weekly religious attendance and a modeled religious-attendance index, both built from national survey data rather than any count of who actually shows up locally, rank 49th of 50. Read together, a chunk of what makes this ward look both remarkably strong and remarkably weak comes from the same estimating method rather than a fact about the neighborhood itself.
reading_the_rankings: Two of Ward 43's last-place rankings need a second look before either reads as a verdict on the neighborhood. The depression ranking, 21.89 percent and dead last of fifty, traces back to a data file with no listed source and no description attached, the thinnest paper trail of any number in this report, layered on top of the usual gaps in which wards this measure even covers. Street light repair time carries the same dead-last rank, but the number behind it is 3.16 days to close a request, fast by any ordinary city standard. Ward 43 loses that ranking because all forty-nine other wards close the same request even faster. Dead last on a measure like that says as much about how quick the rest of Chicago is as it does about this ward.

news.headline: Lincoln Park's Roger Brown Home, 2 Historic DePaul Buildings Get Landmark Protection
news.note: City Council approved landmark status for artist Roger Brown's former home and studio and two historic DePaul University buildings in Lincoln Park.

news.headline: Noisy Electronic Music Fest Riles Lincoln Park Neighbors, Could Prompt Future Ward-Wide Ban
news.note: Residents complained about hours of loud bass and litter from the Lakeshore Music & Arts Festival, raising the possibility of a ward-wide ban on similar events.

news.headline: Lincoln Park Neighbors Say They Weren't Warned Ahead Of Pride Parade Towing Bonanza
news.note: Neighbors disputed the city's claim that no-parking signs for the Pride Parade route were posted with enough notice before their cars were towed.

news.headline: Lincoln Park Late-Night Bars Could Face Crackdown After 'Shocking' Fatal Shooting
news.note: A fatal shooting near a late-night bar strip on Lincoln Avenue, weeks after a nearby shooting wounded a woman, renewed calls for tighter restrictions on late-night business licenses.
